impact_assessment.why: The user asked for a new game with a UI that six independent model providers will review; a deterministic browser puzzle with a pure engine makes both gameplay and visual QA reproducible.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Plan: contain static server paths and correct UI review provenance before publish

impact_assessment.why: Pre-push analysis found that the dev server's prefix containment check could admit a sibling directory whose name starts with the project folder, and one UI history reviewer field overstated which providers completed the final round.
impact_assessment.benefits: Static serving is strictly confined to the project root, the regression is covered by a fast test, and the committed review evidence matches what actually happened.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no gameplay or visual change; dependency: none, Node standard library only; concurrency: none; state: ui_history reviewer field corrected in place
impact_assessment.mitigation: Export the path resolver behind a main-module guard, cover traversal and sibling-prefix cases, correct the record, rerun all project gates and clean-worktree checks, then publish.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: add a one-click launcher that starts the local server and opens the game in the browser, with Windows and POSIX entry points, browser-command tests and README instructions

impact_assessment.why: Opening index.html directly blocks ES modules, so the title screen renders but the Play button does nothing; the user asked for a one-click start button instead of a manual server command.
impact_assessment.benefits: play.cmd and play.sh start the server and open the default browser; npm start also opens the browser; a port-in-use check reopens an already running game instead of failing.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: serve.mjs CLI gains --open, package.json start changes; dependency: Node standard library only, no new packages; concurrency: an existing listener on port 4173 must not be replaced or killed; state: localStorage origin stays on port 4173 so saves remain intact.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the fixed port, detect an existing Prism Relay response before opening, never kill a listener, test the pure browser-command mapping, and verify both launchers and the server without spawning a browser in tests.

handoff.next: implement --open and browserCommand in scripts/serve.mjs with tests
